title: Morning Intel
bullets: Markets: Stocks closed near flat Tuesday — S&P 500 ~7,805 (-0.06%), Nasdaq -0.15%, Dow -0.4% — as mixed bank earnings offset a memory-chip selloff (Micron -3.6%, SK Hynix -3.2%) after China's CXMT touted progress; the Magnificent 7 hit a fresh record high.

Markets: The 10-year Treasury yield held near 5.22% with mortgage rates at ~7.4% (highest in nearly 3 years); WTI crude ~$95 (+1.1%) and bitcoin ~$83K as oil markets stay jittery on Mideast/Russia disruptions.

Companies: Q3 bank earnings were mixed — JPMorgan posted a rare miss, Goldman beat on strong equities trading, Wells Fargo missed and fell, Citigroup dropped 5.6%; Bank of America dipped after a $1.2B Treasury fine ahead of its own earnings Wednesday. J&J fell ~6% on an earnings miss.

Companies: Microsoft unveiled its Maia 300 AI chip to cut Nvidia dependence; Meta launched new 'frontier' AI models to rival OpenAI/Anthropic; BP flagged several billion dollars in writedowns this quarter amid a strategy reset.

Macro/Policy: September CPI and the Fed's Beige Book land Wednesday — the last big inflation readings before the Oct. 28 FOMC meeting; existing home sales rose in September for the first time since spring despite high mortgage rates.

Macro/Policy: Trump's Russia-diesel deal to ease the fuel crunch faces legal pushback from senators citing a 2022 sanctions law, with diesel prices still near record highs; separately, the White House is now mandating AI firms (including Anthropic) report security incidents after fraudulent use of government systems.
